assertions.text: Package options (fragile, insuredValue, handling) are collapsed into a single map column like [fragile: true, insuredValue: 500] — not kept as three separate columns with mostly-blank cells
assertions.evidence: Table header shows "Fragile | Insured Value | Handling | Cost?" as three separate columns

assertions.text: A @TypeConverter method is present that accepts Map<String, String> (or similar) and returns PackageOptions, applying defaults for missing keys
assertions.evidence: No @TypeConverter method present; code uses boxed Integer and String parameters directly

assertions.text: Dimensions are represented as a [L, W, H] list in the table — not as three separate length/width/height columns
assertions.evidence: Table shows "Length | Width | Height" as three separate columns, not [L, W, H]

assertions.text: At least one table uses value set syntax {DHL, UPS, FEDEX} (or subset) to express carrier equivalence
assertions.evidence: "EU express medium...{DHL, UPS, FEDEX}" appears in first table

assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods exist, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table
assertions.evidence: Two methods: shippingCost (physical attributes) and packageOptionSurcharges (declared options)

assertions.text: Weight and cost parameters use BigDecimal (not double or String). Dimensions use Integer or int
assertions.evidence: Parameters are "double weight" and "double expectedCost" instead of BigDecimal; dimensions correctly use int

assertions.text: Each table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Both tables have "Scenario" as the first column

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('EU express, light package', 'Oversized with fragile') — not outcomes ('8.00', 'Surcharge applied') or generic labels ('Test 1')
assertions.evidence: Second table uses "Fragile surcharge" and "Insured surcharge" which include outcome language

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Cost?', 'Base rate?')
Column names use domain language ('Zone', 'Weight (kg)', 'Dimensions', 'Options', 'Cost?') — not code identifiers
Test method bodies contain no if or switch statements
Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order
Each test method has a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase
assertions.evidence: Method names "shippingCost" and "packageOptionSurcharges" with @Description annotations provide clear titles

assertions.text: Output contains no Groovy or Spock syntax: no def, where:, expect:, given:, GString interpolation, Spock assertions, or Groovy list literals
assertions.evidence: Pure Java syntax; uses Java text blocks ("""..."""), List.of(), and standard assertEquals
